Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up: Subprocessors & security next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap + next steps on the security/compliance items we discussed during the discovery call: 

- Scope: Acme indicated HIPAA-regulated data in scope for the pilot, plus GDPR data residency concerns for EU customers.
- Ask from your side: SOC 2 Type II report, full subprocessor list + data flow mapping, and to initiate the vendor security questionnaire (OneTrust).

What I’ve attached here: 
- subprocessor_list_20260227.pdf — current third-party vendors we rely on (compute, logs, monitoring, analytics).
- soc2-summary-2025.pdf — high-level SOC 2 summary (we can provide the full Type II under NDA).

Short answers up front: 
- Primary compute: AWS (us-west-2).
- Backups & DR: geo-replicated (us-west-2 / us-east-1).
- Encryption: data at rest AES-256, in transit TLS1.2+.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Can you confirm whether you want us to fill your OneTrust questionnaire or send the team a link for us to complete?
2) I’ll loop in our security lead and SRE (cc’ing them when required) and schedule a 30-min security deep-dive the week of Mar 2 to run through the subprocessor mapping and data flows.

If that sounds good I’ll go ahead and schedule the call and prepare the detailed subprocessor mapping (including which subprocessors handle PII/PHI).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams: 

- We need a subprocessor mapping that shows where customer data lives and which systems process PII/PHI (including any analytics or monitoring pipelines). Can you provide a per-subprocessor data classification (PII/PHI/aggregated/non-personal)?
- Can you confirm which cloud providers are used for compute, storage, and analytics? Are backups geo-replicated and where are they stored?
- We use OneTrust for vendor questionnaires — can your team either (a) fill our OneTrust link, or (b) take a spreadsheet export and send it back? Which will be faster for you?

Also, our legal team needs to see a copy of the SOC 2 Type II — the summary is helpful but they will request the full report (we can share an NDA link if needed).

If you can get the subprocessor mapping and tell us the preferred questionnaire flow by EOD Wednesday (Mar 4), that will keep procurement on track for our internal review.

Best,
Alex

Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: Subprocessors & security next steps

Alex — thanks, great questions. I’ve pulled the more detailed mapping and answers below and attached the spreadsheet for your procurement/security team to ingest.

High-level answers: 
- Cloud providers: Primary compute and model serving: AWS (us-west-2). Object storage (customer files, logs): AWS S3 (KMS-managed encryption by default). Analytics aggregation and non-prod analytics: GCP (BigQuery) — we do not store customer PII in the analytics pipeline.
- Backups & DR: Backups are geo-replicated between us-west-2 and us-east-1 (encrypted at rest). Snapshots are retained per our retention policy (we’ll include retention windows in the attached mapping).
- Data classification: The attached subprocessor_mapping_20260302.xlsx includes a per-subprocessor column indicating PII/PHI/system-of-record status.
- Encryption & keys: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit. We offer customer-managed KMS for enterprise Private deployments; for hosted accounts we use our KMS with strict access controls. See encryption-practices.pdf for details.
- SOC 2: Full SOC 2 Type II is available under NDA — I’ve attached a redacted copy for your immediate review (redwood_soc2_type2_2025-redacted.pdf) and the summary we sent earlier.

Vendor questionnaire: We can do whichever is fastest for you. Two options: 
1) You send the OneTrust link and we’ll have our security team fill it directly (usually faster for structured fields).
2) We complete the attached spreadsheet export and return it. 

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-min security deep-dive on Mar 4 or Mar 5 (please share any preferred times).
- If you prefer the OneTrust flow, please share the link and a scope (which modules you need completed). Otherwise we’ll complete the attached spreadsheet and return it by EOD Wed (Mar 4).

Attaching: subprocessor_mapping_20260302.xlsx, encryption-practices.pdf, redwood_soc2_type2_2025-redacted.pdf

Thanks — cc’ing Dev and Rachel to own any technical/security answers on the call.

Marissa Cole
